Maya: quick q: experimenting with ephemeral proxy tokens (short-lived JWTs) for service-account routing — want to route by claim 'route_to' instead of org/project header. Anyone tried this with quota attribution?
Ben: we tried something on staging. main issue is attribution -> billing needs project id. if token lacks project claim we fall back to origin header and end up misattributing.
Raj: could we add project claim in the minted token from Console? that would require the minting flow to know the target project at mint time.
Maya: yep. but some clients mint tokens server-side without project context. thinking of doing an exchange: client calls /mint-exchange with org+proj -> returns ephemeral token with claims. pros/cons?
Claire: exchange is more explicit and safer. but UX hit — extra call + latency. also we need telemetry to detect clients that don't adopt exchange.
Ben: we added metrics for this: auth.exchange.success and auth.no_project.fallback. super useful for tracking adoption. also sample log format we've been using: ```auth: issuing token {sub: 'svc-foo', route_to: 'gpu-pool-2', project: 'proj-123'}```
Maya: thinking about quota enforcement: should we check quota on the token's project claim or the origin header? curious about race conditions if both are present/contradict.
Raj: enforce on the claim when present — treat the token as authoritative. if absent, use origin header but mark the request as "unverified" and apply stricter rate limits / lower quotas.
Claire: we should surface attribution confidence in Console. propose a column in per-route dashboards: attribution_confidence = High|Low, and a sampling toggle to capture examples for auditing.
Ben: +1. also need a rollback path: when exchange failures spike, route to fallback model variant to avoid user-facing outages. propose a canary flag `auth_proxy.exchange_required` for rolling the requirement.
Maya: implementation plan draft: 1) mint/exchange endpoint + telemetry, 2) server routing honors claim if present, 3) Console UX for attribution confidence + sampling, 4) quota enforcement rules and stricter fallback. any objections?
Raj: one more edge: multi-tenant proxy tokens — ensure tokens aren't replayable across projects. recommend including `aud` claim = <service_name>:<route_id> and short ttl.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canaries started for auth-proxy/exchange v1 -> 3 hosts. watch: auth.exchange.success, auth.exchange.latency, auth.no_project.fallback.
Maya: thanks. @Ben can you share the grafana query/dashboard so I can add it to the canary checklist?
Ben: sure — grafana: http://grafana/reddash/d/abc123/auth-exchange?orgId=1  (example)
Ben: quick query: sum(rate(auth_exchange_success[5m])) by (env) and sum(rate(auth_no_project_fallback[5m])) by (env)
Claire: :thumbsup: I'll sketch a console mock for the confidence column and ping PM for wording.
Maya: ok i'll start the PR for the exchange endpoint and include the telemetry counters. keeping this thread for decisions/links. plan to ship opt-in by next week.
